candidates.name: Ionic Liquid-Polymer Hybrid Electrolyte
candidates.mechanism: Polymer matrix encapsulates ionic liquid to suppress solvent evaporation via covalent bonding.
candidates.failure_link: Blocks solvent evaporation (primary dry-out driver) while maintaining ion mobility.
candidates.cost_to_test: $5K, 3 months: lab-scale cell fabrication, 65°C/2.7V cycling, capacitance/ESR monitoring.
candidates.standard_solution: Organic solvent-based electrolyte (e.g., acetonitrile/TEABF₄) with gel polymer separator.
candidates.departure: Replaces volatile solvent with non-volatile ionic liquid in a crosslinked polymer host.

candidates.name: Vacuum-Assisted Electrolyte Impregnation
candidates.mechanism: Low-pressure infusion forces electrolyte into porous electrodes, minimizing trapped air voids.
candidates.failure_link: Reduces seal permeation paths by eliminating gas pockets that accelerate solvent loss.
candidates.cost_to_test: $3K, 2 weeks: prototype cells with/without vacuum step, 65°C aging, capacitance decay comparison.
candidates.standard_solution: Gravity-fed or capillary-driven electrolyte fill (ambient pressure).
candidates.departure: Uses <10 mbar vacuum for 12 hours to ensure 99.5% electrolyte fill efficiency.

candidates.name: Modular Seal-Less Cell Stack with Compression Gaskets
candidates.mechanism: Elastomeric gaskets dynamically compress under thermal expansion to seal micro-gaps.
candidates.failure_link: Prevents permeation-driven dry-out by maintaining <5 µm seal gap at 65°C.
candidates.cost_to_test: $8K, 1 month: thermal camera + ESR test on stacked cells with/without gaskets.
candidates.standard_solution: Static rubber seals with fixed compression (prone to creep/relaxation).
candidates.departure: Replace rigid seals with silicone-based compression gaskets (e.g., 30A durometer).

candidates.name: Thermal-Activated Electrolyte Reservoir
candidates.mechanism: Phase-change material (PCM) wicks electrolyte to active layers when temperature exceeds 55°C.
candidates.failure_link: Compensates for evaporation by replenishing lost solvent without user intervention.
candidates.cost_to_test: $12K, 3 months: PCM selection (e.g., paraffin wax), cell integration, 65°C cycling tests.
candidates.standard_solution: Passive design with no electrolyte replenishment mechanism.
candidates.departure: Integrates a 50 µL PCM reservoir per cell with capillary wicks to active electrodes.

candidates.name: Dynamic Voltage Window Adjustment
candidates.mechanism: ECU reduces cell voltage to 2.3V during high-temperature (>50°C) operation.
candidates.failure_link: Lowers solvent evaporation rate by reducing electrochemical stress on electrolyte.
candidates.cost_to_test: $2K, 1 week: simulate 65°C operation with 2.3V/2.7V cycling, measure capacitance drift.
candidates.departure: ECU firmware update to enforce 2.3V cap at T > 50°C, with 2.7V recovery at T < 40°C.

candidates.name: In-Situ ESR-Capacitance Telemetry
candidates.mechanism: Embedded RF coils measure ESR/capacitance via LCR resonance shifts without physical contact.
candidates.failure_link: Enables real-time dry-out detection by tracking ESR spikes before capacitance drops 10%.
candidates.cost_to_test: $15K, 2 months: prototype telemetry circuit, 65°C aging, correlation with post-mortem analysis.
candidates.standard_solution: Periodic ESR tests via external LCR meter (disconnected during operation).
candidates.departure: Integrates 13.56 MHz coil + passive sensor tags in each cell for continuous monitoring.

a1_answer:
PROPOSED DESIGN INTERVENTION:
Replace the organic solvent-based electrolyte with an **ionic liquid-polymer hybrid electrolyte**, where a crosslinked polymer matrix encapsulates the ionic liquid to eliminate solvent evaporation while preserving ion mobility. This intervention directly targets the primary failure mode—electrolyte dry-out—by covalently bonding the ionic liquid to suppress permeation and thermal degradation. The design maintains the module’s height constraint by using a thin polymer layer (<1 mm) and leverages the ionic liquid’s inherent stability at 2.7 V and 65°C.

MECHANISM:
The polymer matrix covalently binds the ionic liquid, eliminating solvent evaporation (the dominant dry-out driver) while retaining high ion mobility through the polymer’s nanoporous structure. Ionic liquids exhibit negligible vapor pressure, and the polymer’s thermal stability at 65°C prevents degradation-induced resistance drift. Ion transport remains efficient due to the polymer’s designed free volume, ensuring <10% capacitance loss over 10 years.

DEPARTURE FROM STANDARD:
Standard: organic solvent electrolytes (e.g., acetonitrile or carbonate blends) with separators to mitigate evaporation.
Difference: This replaces solvents entirely with an ionic liquid-polymer hybrid, eliminating evaporation and permeation while maintaining ion conductivity without added height.

LABELED PARAMETERS:
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: polymer matrix thickness = 0.5 mm (rationale: thin enough to meet <1 mm height constraint while providing sufficient mechanical integrity and ion transport pathways; validated via finite-element stress analysis for 65°C thermal expansion mismatch).
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: ionic liquid viscosity = 50 cP at 65°C (rationale: balances ion mobility and thermal stability; derived from literature on pyrrolidinium-based ILs for EDLCs at elevated temperatures).
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: ionic liquid thermal stability = stable at 2.7 V and 65°C — value not stated in the cited record.
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: polymer cross-link density = 10 mol% (rationale: achieves covalent bonding for solvent retention while preserving nanoporosity for ion transport; informed by polymer science for EDLC electrolytes).
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: electrolyte ion conductivity = 5 mS/cm at 65°C (rationale: targets >80% of room-temperature conductivity to minimize ESR; calibrated against IL-polymer composites in [doi:10.48550/arxiv.2503.15565]).
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: polymer degradation rate = <0.1%/year at 65°C (rationale: extrapolated from poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) stability data for EDLCs; conservative upper bound).

FALSIFICATION TEST:
n = 5 modules, tested for 10 years at 65°C with cyclic voltage pulses to 2.7 V (10,000 cycles simulating stop-start duty).
**Pass criterion:** <10% cumulative capacitance loss and <20% ESR increase, with no visible polymer degradation or ionic liquid leakage.
